claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - Alex, who I'm looking after. He's 8 years old and lives with me at home. I wanted to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him and/or pay for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm primarily responsible for him. He lives with me at home and I take care of his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually he has been in local authority care for a few months now. He doesn't come home regularly though - he's there full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. I need to understand this situation better:

**How many weeks has Alex been in local authority care? Has it been more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been about 12 weeks now that he's been in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information. I have one more key question:

**Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or does he spend 2 nights in a row each week or 7 days or more in a row at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home that much. He stays at the care home full-time, so he's not spending 24 hours a week with me or coming home for those longer periods you mentioned.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider your situation based on the rules:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- You are primarily responsible for Alex ✓
- However, Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks (more than 8 weeks)
- Alex does not spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you
- Alex does not spend 2 nights in a row each week or 7 days or more in a row at home

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child goes into care for more than 8 weeks, Child Benefit payments are usually affected. There is an exception if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, but since Alex stays at the care home full-time and doesn't meet these conditions, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on your circumstances, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

While you meet the basic requirements (living in the UK and being responsible for Alex), the fact that he has been in local authority care for 12 weeks (which is more than the 8-week limit) means you're no longer entitled to Child Benefit. This would only continue if Alex was spending at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or having regular overnight stays, but since he's in care full-time, these exceptions don't apply.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future and he begins spending more time at home with you, you may want to contact HMRC to see if you could claim Child Benefit again at that point.
